transcript: Honestly, I was skeptical at first when they told me a young fellow would come and help us. But Arjun has been a pleasant surprise. He comes in before me every morning, already has the daily production numbers ready on a sheet. I don't have to ask. Last month there was a big issue — our packing line supervisor quit suddenly and we had two big orders due. Arjun stepped in, coordinated with the packing team directly, made a temporary schedule, and both orders went out on time. I didn't even know he had done this until my production manager told me. He doesn't come running to me with every small problem. He figures it out. The team has started going to him with things too — not just me. I think that's a good sign. One thing I'd say is I'm not sure how much of the system he's built will survive after he leaves. He's made a WhatsApp group for daily updates which works, but I don't know if people will keep using it once he's not there to push it. But overall I'm very happy.

Priya is okay. She comes on time, does what we ask her to do. We asked her to help with the attendance system and she did set it up. It works. But I feel like she only does what she's told. I have to give her specific tasks. She doesn't come to me saying 'I noticed this problem, should I work on it?' I have to identify the problem and then hand it to her. She's good at executing once she has instructions but the thinking part, the diagnosis part, I don't see it. The team likes her personally, she's friendly. But in terms of impact on how we work — I can't say I see a big difference yet. We're two months in. Maybe it takes time. She did help us fix a payroll calculation error that was causing issues for a long time — that was good. But that was something we brought to her, she didn't find it herself.

I don't know where to start. Karan is just — I don't know if he's the right fit. He comes in, sits at the desk, works on his laptop. When I ask him what he's doing he says he's documenting something. But I don't see any output. My team members have told me he sometimes disappears for an hour or two and nobody knows where he is. Last week we had a quality issue on the shop floor — defect rate went up suddenly. I expected him to be on top of this, to go and investigate. He didn't. My production manager had to handle it. When I asked Karan about it later he said he hadn't been informed. But it was visible on the shop floor — you just needed to walk around. I'm not sure he understands what we actually do here. He speaks well in meetings but there's no follow through. I've started to wonder whether to keep him for the remaining two months or ask DeepThought to replace him.
